messages.content: Can you retrieve the status information for the gigabitethernet interface on node 42 in the Quartz fabric?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to retrieve status information for the gigabitethernet interface on node 42 in the Quartz fabric. We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate params.

We need to provide url and params. The url should be something like 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo' but we don't have IP. In previous examples, they used placeholder {ip}. But maybe we can use a generic placeholder or ask for IP? The instruction says: "Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax." So we just need to produce a function call. The function signature expects url: string, params: object with optional keys: fabricName, nodeId, podId, interfaceType, infoType.

So we will call:

{
  "url": "https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo",
  "params": {
    "fabricName": "Quartz",
    "nodeId": 42,
    "interfaceType": "gigabitethernet",
    "infoType": "status"
  }
}

We might also include podId if needed, but not necessary. We'll leave it out.

Thus we output a JSON object with those fields.
